facts.fact: USAID's DECA, citing the 2019 USAID and MEASURE Evaluation report on the rollout, states that by September 2019 the health ministry (MSDS) had deployed DHIS-2 in 98 percent of community health centers; it gives the share as deployment, with no numerator or denominator and no statement of who keys the data.

USAID's DECA states that DHIS-2, described as an aggregate data warehouse passing data from health facilities to higher authorities, was rolled out from June 2016 and by September 2019 was deployed in 98 percent of community health centers, the base of the health pyramid; other tiers are not enumerated.

USAID's DECA states that the Government of Mali, in partnership with USAID, began the DHIS-2 rollout in June 2016 to replace an outdated system and that the health ministry (MSDS), in partnership with USAID, maintains it; the report calls DHIS-2 Mali's national health information system.

ANTIM told USAID's DECA team in July 2022 that it had digitalized a dozen of the 65 reference health centers and was working to digitalize 5 of the 13 hospitals, and the report says ANTIM put the hospital information system OpenClinic GA into some community health centers, with 20 more hoped for by the end of 2022.

USAID's DECA states that ANTIM introduced OpenClinic GA, with solar panels and PiBox mini servers, into some community health centers, without giving their number, and that ANTIM hoped by the end of 2022 to reach 20 additional community health centers (ANTIM interview, July 2022).

USAID's DECA states that the health ministry's agency ANTIM introduced and runs the OpenClinic GA deployments in community health centers, reference health centers and hospitals (ANTIM interview, July 2022).

USAID's DECA states that ANTIM's initiatives putting solar panels, PiBox mini servers and OpenClinic GA into community health centers were launched with support from Global Affairs Canada; no domestic budget line is mentioned and the date is that of the ANTIM interview.
